title: Can You Be Jewish Without Being Religious?

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Can you be Jewish without being religious? Yes.
scenes.on_screen: IDENTITY IS NOT A SINGLE CHECKBOX

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Here’s where the one-box explanation breaks down. Jewish identity can involve religion, family, culture, history, or several of those together.

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: Pew’s twenty-twenty survey of Jewish Americans documented that variety. Some people described their Jewish identity through religion. Others connected through ancestry or culture.

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: That doesn’t mean everybody agrees about identity. It means one label does not tell you a person’s beliefs, daily routines, or opinions. You still have to ask.
scenes.on_screen: ONE LABEL DOES NOT DEFINE A PERSON

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: So a Jewish person you see online is not automatically speaking for every Jewish person. And they don’t have to pass your stereotype checklist.
scenes.on_screen: NO ONE PERSON SPEAKS FOR EVERYONE

scenes.speaker: Alex
scenes.text: Curious about someone? Try “What does that mean to you?” Then actually listen to the answer.
scenes.on_screen: ASK: WHAT DOES THAT MEAN TO YOU?

scenes.speaker: Maya
scenes.text: More conversation. Fewer assumptions. People aren’t dropdown menus.
scenes.source: Beyond the Myth · Facts, not scapegoats
